patient_information: A 28-year-old West African man from Ghana.
chief_complaint: A painful ulcer on his left ankle.
history_of_present_illness: The ulcer has been present for 4 months and is not healing; he had a previous ulcer on his right ankle some years ago which took about a year to heal, and he also complains of pain in his right thigh and in both knees.
exposure_and_epidemiology: In the West African context, sickle cell disease is the most likely diagnosis for hereditary haemolytic anaemias.
vitals: Temperature 36.6°C, pulse 88 bpm, blood pressure 110/70 mmHg.
physical_exam: The patient is short for an adult, pale, and has a tinge of jaundice; the ulcer is on his left ankle, next to the medial malleolus, with hyperpigmented skin surrounding it; there is tenderness in both knee joints and his right thigh.
labs_and_diagnostics: A full blood count and peripheral blood film were done, a sickling test was positive, haemoglobin electrophoresis showed a homozygous HbSS-type, a wound swab grew Pseudomonas species sensitive to levofloxacin, and radiography showed a periosteal reaction with slightly sclerotic bones.
differential_diagnosis: Venous ulcer, hereditary haemolytic anaemias (thalassaemia, sickle cell disease, spherocytosis, pyruvate kinase deficiency), tropical ulcer, diabetic ulcer, chronic osteomyelitis, Buruli ulcer, other mycobacterial infections, pyoderma gangrenosum, and malignant diseases.
management_and_clinical_course: Managed with alternate daily wound dressing using normal saline irrigation and povidone-iodine, systemic antibiotic treatment for Pseudomonas, conservative management of recurrent bone pain with good hydration, treatment of infections, daily folic acid supplementation, and pain relief with paracetamol and tramadol; however, the ulcer was still not healed after 3 and 6 years, and skin grafting was under consideration.
final_diagnosis: Sickle cell disease with a chronic ankle ulcer.

images.caption: The patient's left leg showing an ulcer surrounded by hyperpigmented skin on the medial malleolus.
Patient's blood film: irreversibly sickled cells (S), polychromasia (P), target cells (TC), nucleated red cells (NRC) – note similarity with lymphocyte (L). Adequate platelets.
